evidence: The hunk shows the SHA-pin rationale still says 'this step receives DEEPSEEK_API_KEY' while the same diff adds 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}' to that step, so the security comment understates what the step holds. The PR merged two seconds after creation, before the review posted, and the thread got no reply.
guidance_note: When adding a secret input to a step, re-read every comment in that file that lists the step's secrets and update it in the generator (install.sh) in the same change.

evidence: The reviewer correctly notes the file's own LOAD-BEARING comment documents the Actions/Dependabot split-store rule for DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and the new secret was not added to it; whether install.sh actually provisions CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN into the Dependabot store is not shown in the packet. The comment gap is real; the silent-failure outcome is unverified.
guidance_note: When a file documents a per-secret provisioning invariant, extend that documented invariant (and the provisioning in install.sh) to every new secret the same diff introduces.

narrative: One-line CI change adding CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to the review step and bumping the action pin. It merged two seconds after creation, so the review's two advisory findings landed on an already-merged PR and were never answered. Both findings were documentation gaps about the newly added secret: the SHA-pin rationale and the Dependabot dual-store comment still named only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.
guidance_observations: Merging before the reviewer posts means findings are never weighed; the advisory comment gaps here would have been a one-edit fix in install.sh.
A secret added to a generated workflow should be swept against every comment in that file that enumerates secrets, since those comments carry security and provisioning invariants.

evidence: The reviewer raised a conditional risk (install.sh's template may still hold the old SHA and revert the bump). The agent says dotfiles commit cf8cf30 set ACTION_REF to the byte-identical SHA 669c4ea7..., but that commit lives in another repo and the packet cannot confirm it.
guidance_note: When bumping a generated file whose owner lives in another repo, cite the owner-repo commit in the PR body so the reviewer can see the generator moved first.

narrative: Single-line SHA bump of the review action in a generated workflow. The reviewer asked whether the owning install.sh had been bumped too; the agent replied that the dotfiles commit cf8cf30 already carries the same SHA. The claim is specific but cannot be checked from this packet.
guidance_observations: A PR description naming the generator commit would have pre-empted the only finding.

evidence: The diff swaps the SHA pin for '@v1' while the step holds CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, so the mutability risk is real; the tj-actions 'third-party' framing is overstated because promptctl/copirate-code-review-agent is in the same org. The agent conceded the risk, priced the per-release fan-out cost, and cited an owner decision; its 'attacker who can move v1 already controls the org' claim is overstated (repo-level write on the action repo would suffice), but accepting a known tradeoff on the owner's call is a defensible choice.

narrative: The PR moved the review action from a SHA pin to the floating @v1 tag and added persist-credentials: false. The reviewer requested changes on the supply-chain regression. The agent conceded the technical risk and resolved it as an owner-accepted tradeoff, arguing that within one org the trust boundary a SHA pin defends is weak. The reply-hint read 'accept' but the action was a pushback.
guidance_observations: A deliberate security tradeoff is better recorded in the PR body with the owner's decision up front, so a reviewer weighs it instead of flagging it as a regression.

evidence: The reviewer derived 'thirteen' only by assuming the commit made deletions alone; its own facts (10 final entries, 3 deleted) are equally consistent with 12 - 3 + 1. The agent lists the before and after allowlists showing 'Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' was added, and says the entry's own later sentence names that tenth entry. That sentence is not visible in the packet's hunk, so the addition rests on the agent's quoted lists.

narrative: A two-line release promotion of the changelog to 0.6.0. The single finding claimed an arithmetic error in an allowlist count. The agent pushed back with before and after entry lists showing three deletions and one addition. The pushback holds on the logic: the reviewer's inference ignored additions.

evidence: The quoted docs/agent-setup.md section 6 says 'leave the ticket in_progress and report status rather than closing it prematurely', which is about ticket state after a required merge, not permission to abandon a workflow, so the claimed contradiction is weak; the undefined 'handoff' wording is a fair but minor point. The agent reports the owner explicitly rejected a longer version with carve-outs as 'WAY too much text', and correctly argued one-source-of-truth is not at stake for two rules on two subjects.

narrative: A docs-only PR adding an owner-dictated 'workflows run to their end' rule to CLAUDE.md. The reviewer flagged a conflict with the stop-when-in-doubt guidance and asked for carve-outs. The agent declined: section 6 governs ticket honesty, and the owner had rejected the carve-outs. The pushback is sound.

evidence: The original cascadeSurvivors and diffTable compared 'reflect.DeepEqual(issue, want)' on model.Issue, which carries denormalized Labels and a child-derived lifecycle, so a label or child change rewrote the issue and its cascade. Fix 8f3055b introduced issueRowValues as the shared INSERT tuple and diff subject, and added two minimality tests.
guidance_note: Before choosing a whole-value comparison as a 'did this row change' test, check whether the compared type is the persisted row or a hydrated view, and compare the projection the writer binds.

evidence: The new delete helpers duplicated the DELETE text in RemoveRelation, DeleteComment and RemoveLabel, which the agent verified. 8f3055b routed the CRUD callers through the helpers with an (int64, error) return. It left the helpers in export_delta.go, which round 1 flagged as an upward edge (F5), and wrote a 'ONE place its table's DELETE statement lives' comment that later proved false (F10).
guidance_note: When adding a primitive that duplicates existing CRUD SQL, route the old callers through it in the original PR and put the primitive in a file below both layers.

evidence: The comment '[LAW:single-enforcer] the issues column list lives here and nowhere else' is false given CreateIssue's own INSERT INTO issues at store.go:620. 8f3055b replaced it with text naming CreateIssue as the other writer and dropped the citation. The same claim also sat in the CHANGELOG and in writeExportTx's doc, and the fix did not sweep either (F9, and the copy the agent found itself in F10).
guidance_note: When writing a sole-ownership claim, grep the package for every other statement on that table before asserting it.

evidence: The original loop created spine then read with 'DOLT_CHECKOUT -B' and armed the cleanup defer only after the loop, so a failure on the second create stranded the first. 8f3055b arms the defer first and passes a 'created []string' slice to cleanup. The plan had said to delete both unconditionally; the agent built the slice instead, which is better and still the reviewer's suggested fix.
guidance_note: When one atomic resource creation becomes N statements, arm the cleanup before the first statement and have it track what actually exists.

evidence: 8f3055b (the F2 fix) made store.go, labels.go and relations.go call deleteCommentTx, deleteLabelTx and deleteRelationRowTx defined in export_delta.go. The agent checked master and found store.go previously called nothing in the delta layer, so the fix created a back-edge that did not exist before. 277516d moved the helpers to row_deletes.go instead of growing store.go, and the agent named the pre-existing export_delta.go/import_export.go coupling it left alone.
guidance_note: When routing callers through a shared helper, check which file hosts it and whether the new call edges point upward, and relocate the helper in the same fix.

evidence: The 'A reconcile or combine' wording is in the original round-0 hunk, and 8f3055b does not touch CHANGELOG.md, so the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the text predates review. The premise holds, since takeLocalOntoRemoteHead uses the same foldStepper and commitReplayAndAdvance and the 0.5.0 entry names all three paths.
guidance_note: When writing a changelog entry for shared machinery, enumerate every command that drives it, following the precedent of the prior entry in the same area.

evidence: The F1 fix in 8f3055b changed the issues diff to compare issueRowValues, yet the CHANGELOG still said 'the diff compares whole values' and never mentioned the row-versus-view distinction. The agent admitted it 'considered this earlier in the round and talked myself out of it'. 277516d added the sentence.
guidance_note: When a review fix changes documented behaviour, update the changelog entry describing that mechanism in the same commit.

evidence: The scaleHeapGrowthBudget comment is in the original hunk and 8f3055b does not touch the scale test, so the flag is a false positive. Half of the stated ~303 MiB is ~151.5 MiB, so '160 MiB ... well under half the materialized one' is inverted; 277516d replaced the adjectives with the ratios 1.9x and 0.53x.
guidance_note: When a comment justifies a threshold with arithmetic, compute the stated ratios rather than describing them with adjectives.

evidence: The CHANGELOG's 'every INSERT statement still exists in exactly one place' is the same false sole-ownership claim F3 caught in the import_export.go comment, and CreateIssue, AddComment and AddLabel have their own INSERTs. The agent's words: 'I fixed one copy without checking whether the claim had been written down anywhere else'. 277516d narrowed it.
guidance_note: When a reviewer catches a false claim, grep the whole PR (code, changelog, PR body) for the claim and fix every copy in the same commit.

evidence: The 'Each delete below is the ONE place its table's DELETE statement lives' comment was written in 8f3055b (the F2 fix) and moved verbatim into row_deletes.go by 277516d. It is false given setSingleValuedEdgeTx, ClearParent, replaceLabelsTx and the self-edge sweep. 3d7452a narrowed it to by-key single-row deletes, and the agent also fixed a third copy of the INSERT overclaim it found itself in import_export.go.
guidance_note: When a fix writes a 'the one place X lives' comment, grep for every statement of that kind against the table before committing it, rather than carrying the claim across a file move unread.

evidence: The 'which nothing ever resets' text is in the original reconcileScratch doc (round-0 hunk), and 277516d does not touch sync_reconcile.go, so the flag is a false positive. commitReplayAndAdvance calls resetAndLift on the spine, so the claim was false; 3d7452a rewrote it as 'reset exactly once'.
guidance_note: When writing design rationale with an absolute ('never', 'nothing'), check it against the code paths that touch that object, here every reset of the spine.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the duplicated survival predicate predates review, since the original cascadeSurvivors ran 'reflect.DeepEqual(issue, want)' in parallel to diffTable's comparison. The F1 fix kept the two copies in step instead of collapsing them, and added a comment admitting they 'must decide survival by exactly the rule the issues diff uses'. 3886e89 derives survivors from issues.remove, as the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: When a comment has to say two functions must stay in agreement, derive one from the other's output instead of writing the comment.

evidence: The 'LAST edit to touch an issue' assertion is in the original hunk and 3d7452a does not touch it, so the flag is a false positive. With 500 commits over 1000 issues, 'i % issues == i', so no row was ever written twice and last-write-wins was untested. 3886e89 kept the ticket's floors and concentrated edits onto 250 issues through one scaleEditTarget mapping, which neither reviewer option did.
guidance_note: When a test asserts an ordering property, check that the fixture actually produces repeated writes to the same key, so a broken ordering would change the expected result.

evidence: 3d7452a (the F10 fix) rewrote this block to narrow one overclaim and left 'the delta path and the ordinary CRUD commands both route through these' standing over all five helpers, though deleteIssueTx and deleteEventTx have only the delta caller. The agent: 'I rewrote this exact comment one round ago to fix an overclaim ... and left standing a second false universal'. 3886e89 named the 3-of-5 split.
guidance_note: When fixing one overclaim in a paragraph, re-read the whole paragraph for other universal claims before pushing.

evidence: The '70 seconds ... 1.22x, not by 4x' clause is in the original CHANGELOG text and 3886e89 does not touch CHANGELOG.md, so the flag is a false positive. The test runs one scale point with two upper bounds and computes none of those figures. e614aed attributed them to the development machine, and the agent found and narrowed a second false claim, that the wall-clock budget catches the per-step rewrite regression (which projects to about 5.3 minutes, inside the 10-minute bound).
guidance_note: When a changelog sentence follows 'the acceptance test pins', attribute every figure in it either to the test or to an external measurement.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the events diff compared whole IssueEvent values from the original PR, and wholeRow (8f3055b) is the identity, so behaviour was unchanged. queryEvents orders only by 'e.created_at ASC, e.id ASC', leaving the joined change rows unordered under the new DeepEqual comparison. bae4d54 adds 'c.field ASC'; the agent says the PRIMARY KEY (event_id, field) makes that a total order, which matches the reviewer's minimum suggestion.
guidance_note: When introducing a whole-value equality check over data read from SQL, confirm every slice field comes from a query with a total ORDER BY.

narrative: A large perf PR replacing the replay's wholesale rewrite with a row-level delta over a two-branch scratch pair, reviewed over five rounds with 16 findings. Five findings were caused by earlier fixes. The F2 delete consolidation created an upward dependency edge (F5) and a false 'ONE place' comment (F10), and the F10 fix then left a second false universal in the same paragraph (F14). The F1 fix left the changelog describing the old comparison (F7), and the F3 fix narrowed one copy of a sole-ownership overclaim while the changelog copy survived (F9). Every later round also carried findings on original pre-review text (F6, F8, F11, F12, F13, F15, F16), so no round was wholly avoidable, but most of the fix-caused findings were documentation overclaims that a claim-grep would have caught.
guidance_observations: The same false sole-ownership claim surfaced in five places across four rounds; the agent named the lesson itself in round 2 ('grep for the claim, not the file') and still missed a second clause in round 3.
Fix commits that write or move explanatory comments with universal wording ('the ONE place', 'nothing ever', 'both route through') were the main source of fix-caused findings.
Many ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags were false positives on original changelog and comment text, which shows the reviewer reaching unchanged pre-review prose late rather than the fixes causing it.

evidence: The phrase 'quadrupling the chain there, from 127 commits to 502' was written by the #406/F15 fix (e614aed). 502/127 is 3.95x because both counts include scaleFoldedChainOverhead = 2 while the parameter went 125 to 500, exactly 4x. The wording is slightly misleading, as the agent conceded, but it is not wrong at the claimed precision. Declining an edit inside a two-line release promotion is defensible.
guidance_note: When quoting a ratio between two measured counts that include a fixed overhead, state the ratio of the numbers shown or name the parameter that was scaled.

evidence: The bullet describes correctness properties of the delta write path, which #406 introduced and which never shipped in a released binary, so 'Fixed' (which records released bugs) does not fit. The agent conceded that the pre-existing queryEvents ordering clause has the only claim to Fixed and offered a follow-up.

The #406 packet shows 'const scaleFoldedChainOverhead = 2' with the comment that both extra commits 'are replayed like any other', and the agent's F15 reply cites the test asserting 'res.Replayed == scaleFoldedCommits + scaleFoldedChainOverhead'. So 502 is the pinned replay count and 500 is the knob; the reviewer's grep for a literal '502' could not find a computed value.

This batch contains #404, which promoted 0.6.0 dated 2026-08-23 and merged at 14:31Z that day, and #407 itself was created at 19:41Z on 2026-08-23. Both releases were cut the same day, so the shared date is correct.

narrative: A two-line release promotion of #406's changelog to 0.7.0 drew four findings, all declined. Three were wrong: the 502 count includes the replayed overhead commits, 'Fixed' does not fit never-shipped behaviour, and the same-day date matches #404. The fourth, on '127 to 502' not being exactly 4x, points at mildly confusing wording that #406's F15 fix introduced. The agent declined it in favour of a follow-up.
guidance_observations: The '127 to 502' phrasing written during #406's review cost a finding on the next PR; quoting ratios between overhead-inclusive counts invites this.

evidence: import_bulk_test.go lines 49-52 still said 'RankTop, the CreateIssueInput zero value' after the PR flipped the zero value to RankBottom, and Go joins it with the new block into one self-contradictory doc comment. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted and deleted the paragraph in 0409031.
guidance_note: When flipping an enum's zero value, grep for the old constant name and for 'zero value' as well as 'default', since the same claim is phrased several ways.

evidence: This is the same stale 'RankTop, the CreateIssueInput zero value' paragraph as F1, reported by a second scope, and the same 0409031 deletion fixed it.
guidance_note: When flipping an enum's zero value, grep for the old constant name and for 'zero value' as well as 'default', since the same claim is phrased several ways.

evidence: This is a third report of the same stale RankTop doc paragraph, which contradicts the new comment directly below it and store.go's flipped enum; 0409031 deleted it.
guidance_note: When flipping an enum's zero value, grep for the old constant name and for 'zero value' as well as 'default', since the same claim is phrased several ways.

narrative: The PR flips new-ticket placement to bottom-of-frame by swapping the RankPlacement zero value and replacing --bottom with --top. Round 0 reported one stale pre-existing comment three times; the agent deleted it in 0409031, and round 1 approved with no findings. The agent identified why its own sweep missed the comment: the claim was worded 'zero value' rather than 'default'.
guidance_observations: The agent's pre-PR sweep grepped one phrasing of the claim; grepping the old enum constant name (RankTop) would have caught the stale comment before review.
